text: Hi! Tap the green button to keep learning.
Let's do a practice test. Listen to each question, then tap your answer.
Let's practice the ones you missed.
You finished the manual. Great job!
Great job! You're done with Signs.
A stop sign is red. Stop all the way, before the stop line. Let other cars go first. Then go when it is safe.
White signs with black letters tell you the rules. This one is about speed.
A yellow diamond sign is a warning sign. It means danger or a special rule is ahead.
An orange sign means people are working on or near the road.
Green signs help you find places. Blue signs show services, like gas stations.
Yes! Come to a full stop.
The answer is: Come to a full stop.
What does this yellow diamond sign mean?
Danger or a special rule is ahead.
Yes! Danger or a special rule is ahead.
The answer is: Danger or a special rule is ahead.
You see an orange sign. What does it mean?
People are working near the road.
Yes! People are working near the road.
The answer is: People are working near the road.
What does a blue sign show you?
The answer is: Services, like gas stations.
What does a green sign show you?
The answer is: The way to places.
You are the blue car. There is a stop sign. Where do you stop?
In the middle of the crossing.
The answer is: Before the stop line.
Great job! You're done with Yield.
This is a yield sign. Yield means: let cars and people that are coming go first.
When you see a yield sign, slow down as you get close.
If a car is close, stop and wait. Let it go first. When it has passed, you can go.
You are the blue car. There is a yield sign. Who goes first?
The blue car. That is you.
The answer is: The red car.
What should you do when you get close to a yield sign?
What does this sign tell you to do?
Always stop, even with no cars.
Let cars and people go first.
Yes! Let cars and people go first.
The answer is: Let cars and people go first.
Great job! You're done with Traffic lights.
A red light means stop. Stop before the line. Wait until the light is green.
A green light means go. But you still must yield to other cars when needed.
A yellow light means get ready to stop. The light will turn red soon.
A flashing red light is the same as a stop sign. Stop. Let others go first. Then go when it is safe.
This light is red with a green arrow. You may go only the way the arrow points. Here, you turn left. Go only if the way is clear.
You are the blue car. The light is red. What do you do?
Stop. Wait for the green light.
Yes! Stop. Wait for the green light.
The answer is: Stop. Wait for the green light.
You are the blue car. The light is yellow. What does it mean?
The answer is: Get ready to stop.
A red light is flashing. It means the same as what?
The answer is: A stop sign.
You are the blue car. The light is green. What do you do?
Go, but yield to other cars.
Yes! Go, but yield to other cars.
The answer is: Go, but yield to other cars.
You are the blue car. The light is red with a green arrow. Where can you go?
Only the way the arrow points.
Yes! Only the way the arrow points.
The answer is: Only the way the arrow points.
The traffic light is not working. What do you do?
Stop, like at a stop sign.
Yes! Stop, like at a stop sign.
The answer is: Stop, like at a stop sign.
Great job! You're done with Pavement markings.
Yellow lines split cars going opposite ways. You go one way. The red car goes the other way.
White lines split cars going the same way. You and the green car go the same way.
A broken line has gaps. You may cross it to pass the green car. Do it only when it is safe.
Two solid yellow lines mean no passing. Stay in your lane, behind the green car.
At a stop sign, stop before the white stop line. No stop line? Then stop before the crosswalk.
What does a yellow line in the middle of the road split?
The answer is: Cars going opposite ways.
What does a white line between lanes split?
Yes! Cars going the same way.
The answer is: Cars going the same way.
You are the blue car. The white line is broken. When can you change lanes?
The answer is: When it is safe.
You are the blue car. There are two solid yellow lines. What do you do?
Stay in your lane. No passing.
Yes! Stay in your lane. No passing.
The answer is: Stay in your lane. No passing.
You are the blue car. There is a stop sign and a white stop line. Where do you stop?
In the middle of the road.
The answer is: Before the stop line.
You are the blue car. There is a stop sign and a crosswalk, but no stop line. Where do you stop?
In the middle of the road.
The answer is: Before the crosswalk.
Great job! You're done with Right-of-way.
Your light is green. The red car is already in the middle, turning. Let it finish its turn. Then you go.
You want to turn left. The red car comes toward you, going straight. Let it go first. Then you turn left.
You and the red car stop at stop signs at the same time. The red car is on your right. The car on the right goes first. Then you go.
You are leaving a parking lot. Stop before the street. A red car comes from your left. Wait for it to pass. Then turn right.
Your light is red. A person steps into the crosswalk. Now your light turns green. Wait for the person to cross. Then go.
You are the blue car. Who goes first?
The answer is: The red car.
You are the blue car. Who goes first?
The answer is: The red car.
You are the blue car. Who goes first?
The answer is: You, the blue car.
You are the blue car. Who goes first?
The answer is: You, the blue car.
You are the blue car. Who goes first?
The answer is: The red car.
You are the blue car. Who goes first?
The answer is: The person walking.
Great job! You're done with Turns.
Always signal before you turn. Turn on your turn signal at least 100 feet before the turn.
To turn right, get as far right as you can. Then turn into the right lane of the new road.
To turn left, use the lane next to the center line. Turn into the lane next to the center line. Stay on the right side of that line.
You want to make a U-turn. Never start it from the right lane. Use the lane next to the center line. Stay on the left side of that lane. Then make your U-turn.
You want to turn right. Which arrow shows the correct way?
The answer is: The orange arrow.
You want to turn left. Which arrow shows the correct way?
The answer is: The purple arrow.
Which lane can you make a U-turn from?
The lane next to the center line.
Yes! The lane next to the center line.
The answer is: The lane next to the center line.
You want to turn. When must you turn on your turn signal?
At least 10 feet before the turn.
Only as you start to turn.
At least 100 feet before the turn.
Yes! At least 100 feet before the turn.
The answer is: At least 100 feet before the turn.
Great job! You're done with Emergency vehicles.
An ambulance is behind you! Pull over to the right edge of the road, and stop.
Wait until the ambulance goes past you. Then you can drive on.
Pull over and stop for an ambulance, even when it comes toward you in the other lane.
An ambulance is stopped at the side of the road, lights flashing. On a highway with 2 or more lanes your way, move over 1 lane, if it is safe. On every road, slow down.

A blue light on a car means a volunteer firefighter is driving. A green light means a volunteer ambulance worker is driving. Amber lights on snow plows and tow trucks warn you of possible danger. You do not have to yield to them. But it is kind to yield, if it is safe.
You are the blue car. An ambulance with flashing lights is behind you. What do you do?
Pull over to the right and stop.
Yes! Pull over to the right and stop.
The answer is: Pull over to the right and stop.
You are the blue car. You pulled over for an ambulance. When can you drive on?
When it is right behind you.
The answer is: After it passes you.
You are the blue car. An ambulance with flashing lights comes toward you in the other lane. What do you do?
Keep going. It is in the other lane.
Stop in the middle of the road.
Pull over to the right and stop.
Yes! Pull over to the right and stop.
The answer is: Pull over to the right and stop.
You are the blue car, on a highway. An ambulance is stopped at the side of the road, lights flashing. What do you do?
Slow down. Move over 1 lane, if safe.
Speed up to get past it.
Keep going at the same speed.
Yes! Slow down. Move over 1 lane, if safe.
The answer is: Slow down. Move over 1 lane, if safe.
A car has a green light on it. Who is driving?
The answer is: A volunteer ambulance worker.
A tow truck has an amber light on it. What does the amber light do?
Yes! Warns you of possible danger.
The answer is: Warns you of possible danger.
Great job! You're done with School buses.
A school bus is flashing yellow lights. It is getting ready to stop. Slow down, and get ready to stop too.
The school bus has stopped. Its red lights are flashing. You must stop before you reach the bus. Stop at least 20 feet away.
Stay stopped until the bus starts moving again. Then look for children by the side of the road. Drive slowly until you pass them.
A school bus has stopped in the other lane. Its red lights are flashing. You must stop for it too, at least 20 feet away.
This school bus is on the other side of a divided highway. Its red lights are flashing. You must still stop for it.
You are the blue car. The school bus ahead has stopped. Its red lights are flashing. What do you do?
Pass it slowly on the left.
Stop right at its back bumper.
Yes! Stop at least 20 feet away.
The answer is: Stop at least 20 feet away.
You are the blue car. The school bus ahead is flashing yellow lights. What do you do?
Slow down. Get ready to stop.
Honk so it lets you pass.
Yes! Slow down. Get ready to stop.
The answer is: Slow down. Get ready to stop.
You are the blue car. A school bus has stopped in the other lane. Its red lights are flashing. What do you do?
Keep going. It is in the other lane.
Stop before you reach the bus.
Speed up to get past it.
Yes! Stop before you reach the bus.
The answer is: Stop before you reach the bus.
You are the blue car, on a divided highway. A school bus has stopped on the other side. Its red lights are flashing. What do you do?
Keep going. It is on the other side.
Speed up to get past it.
The answer is: Stop for the bus.
You are the blue car. You stopped for a school bus. Its red lights are still flashing. When can you drive again?
Right away, if you see no children.
When the bus starts moving again.
When a car behind you honks.
Yes! When the bus starts moving again.
The answer is: When the bus starts moving again.
You are the blue car. The school bus has driven away. What do you do now?
Speed up to make up time.
Look for children. Drive slowly past them.
Honk so the children stay back.
Drive fast past the bus stop.
Yes! Look for children. Drive slowly past them.
The answer is: Look for children. Drive slowly past them.
Great job! You're done with Speed.
You must obey the speed limit. If there is no speed limit sign, drive no more than 55 miles per hour.
On an expressway, the speed limit is usually 55 miles per hour. In some country areas, the sign can say 65.
It is foggy ahead. The sign says 55 miles per hour. The safe speed is much lower. Slow down.
You are driving very slowly. That can be as dangerous as driving too fast. It gets in the way of other cars.
Some cities have lower speed limits that are not always on a sign. In New York City, the speed limit is 25 miles per hour, if no sign says different.
You are the blue car. There is no speed limit sign. What is the fastest you may drive?
The answer is: 55 miles per hour.
You are the blue car. It is foggy ahead. The speed limit sign says 55. How fast should you drive?
Slower than 55, at a safe speed.
Yes! Slower than 55, at a safe speed.
The answer is: Slower than 55, at a safe speed.
You are the blue car. You are driving very slowly. What is true?
It makes the road safer for everyone.
It can be as dangerous as driving too fast.
It makes other cars go faster.
Yes! It can be as dangerous as driving too fast.
The answer is: It can be as dangerous as driving too fast.
You are driving in New York City. There is no speed limit sign. What is the speed limit?
The answer is: 25 miles per hour.
The speed limit is 65 miles per hour.
Drive at least 65 miles per hour.
Yes! The speed limit is 65 miles per hour.
The answer is: The speed limit is 65 miles per hour.
Great job! You're done with Parking.
Find a space big enough for your car. Check your mirrors and signal. Stop next to the car in front of the space. Leave about 2 feet between the cars.
You are parked next to the curb. Your wheels must be no more than 1 foot from the curb.
This is a fire hydrant. Park at least 15 feet away from it.
This crosswalk is at an intersection. Park at least 20 feet away from it.
This is a STOP sign. Park at least 30 feet away from it. Also park at least 30 feet from a YIELD sign or a traffic light.
You are the blue car. You want to park in the empty space. Where do you stop first?
In the middle of the space.
Next to the car in front of the space.
Next to the car behind the space.
Yes! Next to the car in front of the space.
The answer is: Next to the car in front of the space.
You are the blue car. You stopped next to the car in front of the space. How far from it should you be?
You are the blue car. You parked next to the curb. How close to the curb must your wheels be?
The answer is: No more than 1 foot.
You are the blue car. You want to park near this fire hydrant. How far away must you park?
Right next to it is fine.
The answer is: At least 15 feet.
You are the blue car. You want to park near this crosswalk at an intersection. How far away must you park?
The answer is: At least 20 feet.
You are the blue car. You want to park near this STOP sign. How far away must you park?
The answer is: At least 30 feet.
Great job! You're done with Parking signs.
This sign says No Parking. You may stop for a short time, to load or unload things or people.
This sign says No Standing. You may stop for a short time, only to pick up or drop off people. You must stay in the car.
This sign says No Stopping. You may stop here only to obey a traffic sign, a traffic light, or an officer. Or to avoid a crash with another car.
This space is reserved. You may park here only with a permit or plates for persons with disabilities. The person who got them must be in the car.
Next to it is a space with diagonal stripes. Do not park there. It gives room for people with wheelchairs, and for cars with special equipment.
You are the blue car. You see a No Parking sign. What may you do here?
Park and go to a movie.
Stop a short time to load or unload.
Leave your car here all day.
Nothing. You may never stop here.
Yes! Stop a short time to load or unload.
The answer is: Stop a short time to load or unload.
You are the blue car. You see a No Standing sign. Your friend needs to get out. What may you do?
Stop a short time and let her out.
Nothing. You may never stop here.
Yes! Stop a short time and let her out.
The answer is: Stop a short time and let her out.
You see a No Stopping sign. When may you stop there?
To obey signs, lights, officers, or avoid crashes.
To park for a short time.
Yes! To obey signs, lights, officers, or avoid crashes.
The answer is: To obey signs, lights, officers, or avoid crashes.
This space is reserved for people with disabilities.
Yes! This space is reserved for people with disabilities.
The answer is: This space is reserved for people with disabilities.
Your friend has a permit for persons with disabilities. You drive her car. When may you park in a reserved space?
Any time you drive her car.
Only when your friend is in the car.
When the parking lot is full.
Yes! Only when your friend is in the car.
The answer is: Only when your friend is in the car.
You are the blue car. There is a space with diagonal stripes next to a reserved space. What is the rule?
Park there if you have a permit.
Park there if the lot is full.
The answer is: Do not park there.
Great job! You're done with Alcohol and drugs.
Alcohol makes your driving skills weaker. You react more slowly. You do not see as clearly. You judge speed and distance wrong. You take more chances.
Drugs can make your driving unsafe too. This includes marijuana, illegal drugs, and some medicines from a doctor. Alcohol and drugs together are even worse.
B.A.C. means how much alcohol is in your blood. A B.A.C. of 0.08 or more shows that a driver is drunk.
Only time lowers the alcohol in your blood. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers do not lower it.
You are under 21. You may not drive with any alcohol in your blood that a test can find. Never drive after drinking.
What does alcohol do to your driving?
The answer is: You react more slowly.
You are the blue car. Which of these can make your driving unsafe, like alcohol?
What does a B.A.C. of 0.08 or more show?
The driver is safe to drive.
The answer is: The driver is drunk.
What is the only thing that lowers the alcohol in your blood?
You are under 21. How much alcohol may be in your blood when you drive?
None that a test can find.
Any amount, if you feel fine.
Yes! None that a test can find.
The answer is: None that a test can find.

Chapter 4 is about traffic control, and it starts with signs. Traffic signs tell you about the rules of the road and about special hazards. They also tell you where you are, how to get where you are going, and where you can find services. The shape and the color of a sign give you a clue about what kind of information it has.

There are four main kinds of signs. Regulation signs are normally white rectangles with black letters or symbols. But some regulation signs have different shapes, and some use red letters or symbols. Warning signs are normally yellow and shaped like a diamond, with black letters or symbols. Destination signs are green with white letters and symbols. Service signs are blue with white letters and symbols. Know the signs that come next and what they mean, because you will be asked about them on your written test.

Now for the most common signs, starting with regulation signs. The stop sign is red with white letters. At a stop sign, come to a full stop. Then yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians that are in the intersection or heading toward it, and go only when it is safe. If there is a stop line painted on the road, you must stop before the stop line. If there is no stop line, you must stop before you enter the crosswalk.

What if there is no stop line and no crosswalk? Then you must stop before you enter the intersection. Stop at the point closest to the intersection where you can see the traffic coming along the road that crosses yours.

Next is the yield sign. It is red and white, with red letters. When you see a yield sign, slow down as you reach the intersection. Get ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to vehicles and pedestrians that are in the intersection or heading toward it. If traffic makes it necessary, you must come to a full stop at a yield sign. So when you come up to one, check carefully for traffic, and be prepared to stop.

Other regulation signs are white, with black letters or symbols, red ones, or both. These signs tell you the rules about which direction traffic goes, how to use the lanes, turns, speed, parking, and other special requirements. In the picture you can see a few of them: Do Not Pass, No Turn On Red, and Speed Limit 55.

Some regulation signs show a symbol with a red circle and a slash over it. That means an action is not allowed, like making a right turn, or that some vehicles are not allowed on the road. White rectangle signs with black or red letters or symbols tell you to be alert for special rules.

Now, warning signs. They are yellow, with black letters or symbols. A warning sign means you are coming up to a dangerous spot, or to a place where there is a special rule, like the sample signs in the picture. Sometimes a warning sign has a yellow and black recommended speed sign with it. That means a slower speed is advised in that area.

Work area signs are orange, with black letters or symbols. They mean people are working on the road or near it, and a flag person may be controlling traffic. A work area speed limit as low as 25 miles per hour can be posted. Even if no speed limit is posted, you must drive at a slower speed through the work zone. And you must always obey the flag persons.
These pictures show some of the signals a flag person will use: the signals for stop, for proceed, and for slow. Know these signals and obey them.
Destination signs are green, with white letters. They show the direction and the distance to places. The sign in the picture points left to Rochester, 55, and right to Lockport, 10.

Route signs come in different colors. They mark interstate, U.S., state, or county routes, and the shape of the sign tells you what type of route you are on. In the picture, from left to right, are signs for a state route, a U.S. route, and an interstate route. When you plan a trip, use a highway map to decide which routes to take. Then, during the trip, watch for destination signs, so you won't get lost or have to turn or stop suddenly.
Last are service signs. They are blue, with white letters or symbols. They show you where to find services, like rest areas, gas stations, camping, or medical facilities.

Next, traffic signals. Traffic lights are normally red, yellow, and green, in that order from top to bottom or from left to right. At some intersections, there is just one red, yellow, or green light by itself. Some traffic lights stay steady, and others flash. Some are round, and some are arrows.

State law says what to do if the traffic lights or controls are out of service, or are not working correctly, when you come to an intersection. You must stop, the same way you would for a stop sign. Then go ahead by following the rules of right-of-way, unless a traffic officer tells you to go.

Here is what each light means. A steady red light means stop. Do not go until the light turns green. If a green arrow is showing along with the red light, you can go only in the direction of the arrow, and only if the intersection is clear.

You can turn right at a steady red light, after you come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. You can turn left at a steady red light only when you are turning from a one-way road onto another one-way road. Here too, you must first come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. But there are exceptions, which come next.

You cannot turn at a red light if a No Turn On Red sign is posted, or if another sign, signal, or pavement marking prevents the turn. In New York City, you are not allowed to turn on a red light at all, unless a sign is posted that permits it. And the driver of a school bus with students on it cannot turn right on any red light.
A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. Stop, yield the right-of-way, and go when it is safe.

A red arrow means do not go in the direction of the arrow until the red arrow turns off and a green light or a green arrow turns on. You are not allowed to make a right or left turn on red at a red arrow.
A steady yellow light means be prepared to stop, because the traffic signal is about to turn red. A flashing yellow light means drive with caution.
A yellow arrow means the protection of the green arrow is about to end. If you plan to turn in the direction of the arrow, be prepared to stop.
A steady green light means go. But you still have to yield the right-of-way to other traffic at the intersection, as the law requires.
A green arrow means you can go in the direction of the arrow. But you must still yield the right-of-way to other traffic at the intersection, as the law requires.

Some highways have special lane use control lights above the pavement. They show which lanes can be used at certain times. A steady red X means do not drive in this lane. A steady yellow X means move out of this lane. A flashing yellow X means this lane can only be used for a left turn. And a green arrow means you can use this lane.

Next, pavement markings. The lines and symbols on the road divide the lanes. They tell you when you can pass other vehicles or change lanes. They also tell you which lanes to use for turns, and where you must stop for signs or traffic signals. In the pictures for this part, the arrows show which way the traffic is moving.

Solid lines along the side of the road show you where its edge is. That is where the travel lane ends and the shoulder begins. It is illegal to drive across this edge line, except when a police officer or another authorized official tells you to, or when an official sign allows it. If the edge line angles in toward the center of the road, it means the road gets narrower ahead.

Lines between lanes of traffic going the same direction are white. Lines between traffic going in opposite directions are yellow. There may be two lines between lanes, and the lines can be solid or broken.
Here is what the lines mean. With one broken line, you can pass other vehicles or change lanes, if you can do it safely without getting in the way of traffic.

Sometimes there is a solid line next to a broken line. If you are on the side with the solid line, you cannot pass other vehicles or cross the line, except to make a left turn into a driveway. If you are on the side with the broken line, you can pass, if it is safe and you will not get in the way of traffic.

With double solid lines, you cannot pass or change lanes. You cannot cross the lines, except to turn left to enter or leave the highway. For example, you may cross them to turn into or out of a driveway, or to make a U-turn.
With one solid line, you can pass other vehicles or change lanes, but only when something blocking the road, or the traffic conditions, make it necessary.

Now, stop lines and crosswalks. At an intersection controlled by a stop sign, a yield sign, or a traffic light, there can be a white line painted across your lane, called a stop line. There can also be two parallel lines painted across the road, called a crosswalk, or there can be both. When a sign or a light makes you stop, you must stop before you reach the stop line, if there is one. If there isn't, stop before the crosswalk.

You only have to stop at a stop line or a crosswalk if a light, a sign, or a traffic officer tells you to. You also have to stop there to yield to a pedestrian, an in-line skater, or a scooter at a crosswalk, whether the crosswalk is marked or unmarked.

At some intersections, a single stop line may be placed farther back. This leaves room for larger vehicles, like tractor-trailers, buses, and trucks, to turn without forcing other traffic to back up. It's important that you stop before you reach this stop line.

Arrows on the road show which lanes you must use. In this picture, for example, you can turn right only from the right lane. To go straight, you must use the left lane. You must be in the correct lane before you reach the solid line that separates the lanes.

A diamond symbol marks a reserved lane. These lanes are for buses, for high-occupancy vehicles like car pools and van pools, for bicycles, or for other special vehicles. You cannot enter or use one of these lanes unless your vehicle meets the rules shown on the signs, such as how many people must be riding in it. Those rules apply during the times the signs say they are in effect.

On city streets, parts of the solid white line between a diamond lane and the normal lanes can be replaced by broken white lines. In those places, vehicles that are not high-occupancy vehicles can enter the reserved lane if they make a right turn at the next intersection. Bus lanes and high-occupancy vehicle lanes help make the best use of the limited space on streets and highways. They make sure that the most important vehicles move the fastest.

Last in this chapter, traffic officers. Directions from a traffic officer come before signs, signals, or pavement markings. For example, if a traffic officer signals you to stop at a green light, you must stop. And if an officer signals you to drive through a red light or a stop sign, you must do it.
Many kinds of people are allowed to direct traffic. They include police officers, fire police, highway work area flag persons, school crossing persons, and school bus drivers.
